ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the circuit shown in the figure, the electromotive force of the power supply is $E=60V$, the internal resistance is $r=2\Omega$, and the fixed resistors are $R_1=8\Omega$ and $R_2=15\Omega$. The distance between the two plates A and B of the parallel-plate capacitor is $4\mathrm{cm}$, and the charge on the capacitor at this moment is $6\times10^{-8}\mathrm{C}$. Plate A is grounded (potential is zero).

1. What is the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor?
2. What is the electric field strength between the plates of a parallel-plate capacitor?
3. What is the electric potential at point C, which is 1 cm away from plate B?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure are two horizontal parallel metal plates, labeled A and B, forming a parallel-plate capacitor; plate A is connected to the upper wire and has a grounding symbol, and plate B is connected to the lower wire. In the middle there is a vertical resistor R2 connected between the same upper and lower two nodes, therefore capacitor A-B and R2 are in parallel. In the upper right there is resistor R1, and on the right side is the power supply branch; the power supply has internal resistance r. After the capacitor is charged and stabilized, there is no current in the capacitor branch. Reasoning: When stable, the main circuit current passes only through r, R1, and R2, and the equivalent series resistance is r+R1+R2=2+8+15=25 Ω, so I=E/(r+R1+R2)=60/25=2.4 A. The voltage across R2 is U=IR2=2.4×15=36 V; because the capacitor is in parallel with R2, the voltage between the two plates of the capacitor U_AB=36 V, and the potential of plate A is higher than that of plate B. It is known that the capacitor charge Q=6×10^-8 C, so C=Q/U=6×10^-8/36=1.67×10^-9 F. The plate spacing d=4 cm=0.04 m, and the magnitude of the electric field strength E_field=U/d=36/0.04=900 V/m. Plate A is grounded, V_A=0 V, and V_A−V_B=36 V, so V_B=-36 V. Point C is 1 cm from plate B, namely at 1/4 of the distance from B to A. In a uniform electric field, the potential changes linearly, therefore V_C=V_B+(1/4)(V_A−V_B)=-36+9=-27 V.
